titleDv: ޤާނޫނު ނަންބަރު 9/2009 (ރައީސުލްޖުމްހޫރިއްޔާކަން ކޮށްފައިވާ މީހަކަށް ދޭންޖެހޭ ރައްކާތެރިކަމާއި އިނާޔަތްތަކުގެ ޤާނޫނު) އަށް ... ވަނަ އިޞްލާޙު ގެނައުމުގެ ބިލު
summary: This government bill amends the Former Presidents Protection and Benefit Act (Act No. 9/2009). It scraps Article 8, which lets a former president get up to MVR 175,000 a month from the state to run an office. It extends the law to former vice presidents who completed a full five-year term, giving them MVR 25,000 a month and state-paid medical care in the Maldives and abroad. It also pauses a one-term former president's allowance while they hold another state post or serve a second term, and drops the duty to provide security to a former president while they live abroad.
whyItMatters: The Finance Ministry's attached estimate says the changes would cut spending on these benefits from a budgeted MVR 19.7 million to MVR 10.2 million in 2026, a saving of about MVR 9.5 to 10.6 million a year.
keyProvisions: Clause 4 repeals Article 8, removing the state payment of up to MVR 175,000 a month for a former president's office, staff and related costs.

Clause 5 adds Article 8-1: a former vice president gets MVR 25,000 a month and state-paid medical care at home and abroad, with the monthly payment paused while they hold any elected or appointed state post.
Clause 2 rewrites Article 3(c) so a one-term former president's financial allowance is paused while they serve a second term as president or hold another state post.

Clause 3 adds Article 5(b) and (c): Maldives National Defence Force protection does not have to be given to a former president while they live abroad, but must be arranged when they visit the Maldives.

Clauses 6 and 7 extend Article 9(a) (the government's power to change benefits in an economic crisis, after consulting Parliament) to all beneficiaries, and extend Article 10's loss of all benefits for a crime proven to be committed in office to vice presidents.

Clause 8 adds Article 13(e) defining a former vice president as someone who completed the vice president's term in a five-year presidential term, and clause 9 says the law takes effect when published in the Government Gazette.
whoIsAffected: Former presidents and former vice presidents of the Maldives and their spouses, the MNDF that protects them, and the state budget that pays their benefits.
statedReasons: The government says the bill reviews some benefits given to former presidents under Act No. 9/2009, gives benefits to people who have served as vice president, and makes the related amendments to the law.
